prompt: Dolphins (mammals) and sharks (fish) have very similar streamlined bodies and fins, yet their common ancestor had neither shape. This resemblance is best explained by:

options.text: Convergent evolution: unrelated lineages independently evolving similar solutions to the same challenge of moving fast in water
Both species inheriting the shape unchanged from a recent shared ancestor
Individual dolphins reshaping their bodies during their lifetimes and passing that on

explanation: Similar environments impose similar selection pressures. Dolphins and sharks independently converged on a streamlined form for efficient swimming, despite belonging to very different vertebrate lineages.
